cases.request: Make a review page for the 15 January launch. Lyon and Nantes both have a suitable hall and cost the same. A valid permit on the launch date is a hard requirement. Nantes's permit expires on 31 December; Lyon's is valid through 31 March. The Overview can describe the shared criteria, and a Restrictions section must let me inspect the permits and decide which city is eligible. A navigation button labeled Restrictions must actually open that section.

required_outcomes.criterion: Activating Restrictions reveals the named permit dates and eligible city.
Preserve the 15 January launch requirement and explain which permit satisfies it.

routes.expected: Restrictions becomes visible and Overview becomes hidden.
The keyboard route opens the same Restrictions section.

cases.request: Write one short executive-summary paragraph recommending whether to move web sessions from Redis to Postgres. Preserve the recommendation, the main latency tradeoff, the 30-day dual-write plan, and the go/no-go condition: the database owners must approve 55% peak CPU before proceeding. Supporting notes: Redis is 81% of 64 GB, renewal adds 38%, peak active sessions 312k; 1.9M total sessions, 71% idle over 7 days. Median session read 0.4 ms, p95 1.9 ms, p99 7.8 ms. On 14–27 September the daily p95 values were 1.7, 1.8, 1.8, 3.9, 1.9, 1.8, 1.7, 1.7, 1.8, 4.4, 1.9, 1.8, 1.7, 1.8 ms. Postgres gives immediate logout-everywhere and has 3.1 ms p95; peak CPU reaches 55% against the 70% alert. Recommend Postgres, subject to database-owner approval. Keep this an executive summary; omit raw daily measurements and an appendix.

required_outcomes.criterion: Give a short decision summary, preserving recommendation, latency tradeoff, dual-write plan and explicit owner-approval go/no-go condition.
